name: Auto Queens
description:
Poster design by Jahan Singh Bakshi and Prashant C
Amid dense traffic and long working days, auto-rickshaw drivers Mohana and Leela Rani fight for visibility and respect in Chennai while facing a lack of infrastructure, parking facilities, harassment, and social prejudice. Together with other female drivers, they stand at the forefront of a growing movement of women who are taking the wheel and, step by step, leading a quiet mobility revolution in a male-dominated sector.

Join us for the screening of Auto Queens, and then for a conversation with the producer, Sarabhi Varsini and Mohana, moderated by Sruthi Krishnan on cooperative organising, women's labour, and collective agency.

name: Between the Looms - The Hands that Time Unearthed
Visibilising Labour
description:
Despite sustaining our cities and households, domestic workers, sanitation workers, caregivers, and gig-economy workers continue to be rendered invisible and undervalued. The rise of app-based and platform economies has created new avenues of employment for women, but these spaces also remain fraught with challenges. Women in these sectors continue to face unsafe working conditions, harassment, lack of social security, and inadequate grievance redressal mechanisms. Weak enforcement of labour protections and exploitative work structures further deepen precarity and exclusion.

Focusing on the intersections of labour, gender and violence, this session with Geeta Menon and Poorna Ravishankar will examine how systems of power continue to marginalise women in both domestic and informal workspaces. Bringing together artists, activists, workers, and policy practitioners, the discussion aims to be a space to share experiences, understand currently available legal frameworks, and collaboratively plan what is needed to build stronger protections, safer working environments, collective organising, and more equitable frameworks of labour and dignity.

name: Embodied Language: A Deaf-Led Human Library on warrior garments
description:
Image Credits: Anonymous
Join us for a Human Library led by Rashmi Malhotra, founder of India Deaf Queer, as they share their lived experiences and invite conversations around access, identity, and everyday life. Through this session, we will also reflect on the importance of making cultural spaces more inclusive and accessible.

Inspired by MAP's exhibition warrior garments by afra eisma, the session invites participants to reflect on how emotions, identity, and intersectional experiences are carried and expressed. Through Indian Sign Language (ISL), Rashmi creates a space for dialogue, reflection, and exchange with Deaf and queer audiences. You are welcome to join, listen, ask questions, or simply be present.

Please note: This session will be conducted in Indian Sign Language (ISL) with interpretation into spoken English.

This session is happening as part of the closing weekend of our exhibition warrior garments and Disability Pride programming 2026

name: A Visual Sharing Circle on Trauma, Anger, Care and Boundaries
description:
Image Credits: Anonymous
Join us for a Deaf-led visual sharing circle with Charu Narang, founder of DeafWomenToo (DWT). Inspired by warrior garments, this workshop invites Deaf participants to explore shared memories and lived experiences through guided visual activities, including body mapping and creative expression. Together, we will create space for conversations around trauma, anger, healing, and self-expression in a supportive environment.

Participants are welcome to engage at their own comfort level—whether through making, sharing, reflecting, or simply being present.

Please note: This workshop supports personal reflection and self-expression. It is not a therapy session. The session will be conducted in Indian Sign Language (ISL), with interpretation into spoken English.

This session is part of the closing weekend of our exhibition warrior garments and Disability Pride programming 2026.
